answer: Filecoin proved one disk holds exactly one honest copy: a ballot earns its vote by sealing a unique 1 GB mirror shard of the shared ledger, two hours of disk work no second ballot can reuse. At the jetty, auditors pulse a random ballot each tide and demand one 32 KB slice in 30 seconds — an honest drive answers in a blink. A farm stamping 10,000 ballots from one drive dies by the storage audit: a thousand slices at once choke its read queue, proofs miss the deadline, and $25 bonds burn, $250,000 gone. A borrowed mirror breaks on first use: the farm buys 10,000 drives or loses its stake.
